claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 6749 §4.1.1: response_type "Value MUST be set to 'code'"; client_id, redirect_uri, scope are the request parameters, added "to the query component of the authorization endpoint URI". §4.1.2: the server issues the code "by adding the following parameters to the query component of the redirection URI". Captured step 1 shows .../auth/callback?...&code=...

RFC 6749 §4.1.2 (rfc6749.txt, grep): "The authorization code MUST expire shortly after it is issued to mitigate the risk of leaks. A maximum authorization code lifetime of 10 minutes is RECOMMENDED. The client MUST NOT use the authorization code more than once. If an authorization code is used more than once, the authorization server MUST deny the request."

RFC 6749 §4.1.3: grant_type "MUST be set to 'authorization_code'", code, redirect_uri, client_id, sent with application/x-www-form-urlencoded (POST). §5.1: "The parameters are included in the entity-body of the HTTP response using the 'application/json' media type." RFC 7636 §4.5: code_verifier REQUIRED at the token endpoint. exchange() at oauth-code-flow.sh:38-42 sends exactly these with curl -d (POST).

Keycloak Server Admin Guide (page header 'Version 26.7.4'), Valid Redirect URIs: "Exact (case sensitive) string matching is used to compare valid redirect URIs." donhang-realm.json: redirectUris ["http://localhost:8081/auth/callback"], no wildcard. Captured step 5: "Keycloak shows an error page instead of redirecting: Invalid parameter: redirect_uri" / "-> 400".

RFC 6749 §2.1: public = "Clients incapable of maintaining the confidentiality of their credentials (e.g., clients executing on the device used by the resource owner, such as an installed native application or a web browser-based application)"; user-agent-based application: "a public client in which the client code is downloaded from a web server and executes within a user-agent (e.g., web browser)".

RFC 7636 §4.2: "code_challenge = BASE64URL-ENCODE(SHA256(ASCII(code_verifier)))"; App. A: strip '=', '+'->'-', '/'->'_'.
